details: Bitcoin is trading around $64,700, showing modest gains, supported by a return of institutional demand through spot Bitcoin ETF inflows, which saw $132.3 million in net inflows on July 17. However, the Fear & Greed Index remains at 29, indicating cautious sentiment across the broader crypto market, and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East continue to cap risk appetite.
title: Bitcoin Stabilizes Above $64K as ETF Inflows Return

details: US regulators failed to finalize the implementing rules for the federal stablecoin framework by the July 18 deadline mandated by the GENIUS Act. This regulatory vacuum leaves issuers and exchanges facing unclear compliance timelines ahead of January 2027 enforcement, contributing to persistent policy and security uncertainties in the crypto market.
title: US Regulators Miss Deadline for Final Stablecoin Rules

details: Ethereum is trading near $1,860, extending its recovery and holding above its 50-day Exponential Moving Average (EMA) at approximately $1,818. This suggests buyers are maintaining control in the short term. However, ETH still faces significant resistance from its 100-day EMA at $1,938, which it needs to clear to confirm a stronger bullish reversal. Exchange outflows and increased staking activity are contributing to reduced sell pressure.
title: Ethereum Holds Support, Prepares for Potential Breakout

details: Despite Brent crude surpassing $90 per barrel due to escalating geopolitical tensions between the US and Iran, Bitcoin has remained relatively stable, trading just below $64,700. This indicates a growing divergence, with Bitcoin tracking macro liquidity and rate expectations rather than reacting directly to geopolitical events that typically impact oil prices.
title: Bitcoin Unfazed by Surging Oil Prices Amid Mideast Conflict
